Palladium-catalysed alleneamination of
\gamma .
d-unsaturated hydrazones with propargylic
acetates: access to tetrahydropyridazines bearing
allenes†
Shuaijie Wu,<sup>a</sup> Shiji Xu,<sup>a</sup> Yanru He,<sup>a</sup> Jing Sun,<sup>a</sup> Wei Jiang,<sup>b</sup> Chao-Guo Yan, *<sup>a</sup>
Weiming Hu *<sup>c</sup> and Lei Wang *<sup>a</sup>
A highly eficient palladium-catalysed alleneamination of c,
d-unsaturated hydrazones with propargylic acetates has been
developed. This novel method was used to synthesize tetrahydro-
pyridazines bearing allene derivatives, and did so in moderate to
good yields. This protocol features a simple catalytic system, broad
substrate scope, easy scale-up, and versatile transformations.
Tetrahydropyridazines constitute a class of six-membered
N-heterocycles and represent a privileged motif in various
natural products.<sup>1</sup> Moreover, tetrahydropyridazines and their
derivatives exhibit a large range of pharmacological activities,<sup>2,3</sup>
such as neuro-transmitter inhibitor, antimicrobial, influenza
neuraminidase inhibitor, and cannabinoid CB receptor activ-
ities. In addition, they play an important role in synthetic
organic chemistry as versatile building blocks due to the
presence of an N–N bond (Fig. 1).<sup>4</sup> Therefore, the development
of efficient synthetic methodologies for their preparation has
attracted considerable attention.
Over the past two decades, significant eforts have been
devoted to developing elegant routes toward six-membered
nitrogen-containing heterocycles, including hydrogenation of
pyridine<sup>5</sup> and aza-Diels–Alder reactions (Scheme 1a).<sup>6</sup> Hydra-
zones are key structural motifs and have been widely used in
drug development, materials science, and biological probes.
Meanwhile, the advantages of hydrazones, including their easy
preparation, the presence of an N–N bond, and their role as
synthetic equivalents to ketones or aldehydes enables their
extensive use for synthesizing a range of N-heterocycles.<sup>8–10</sup>
Especially, the hydrazones containing unsaturated C–C double
bonds have been frequently studied for the synthesis of tetra-
hydropyridazines. For instance, Xiao’s, Liu ’s and Stuart’s group
independently realized the synthesis of functionalized tetrahy-
dropyridazines through 6-endo-trig cyclization (Scheme 1b,
left).<sup>9</sup> Afterwards, the Yu and Pan group developed a similar
method that produced sulfonylated tetrahydropyridazines in
moderate to good yields (Scheme 1b, right).<sup>10</sup> In addition, the
Chen and Xiao group<sup>11</sup> in 2017 described Pd(II)-catalysed
aminoarylation reactions of g,d-unsaturated hydrazones, pro-
viding general approaches to tetrahydropyridazines. Later,
Zhang and Zhao reported an efficient Pd(0)-catalysed cycliza-
tion-coupling reaction of readily available g,d-alkenyl hydra-
zone with organohalides for the synthesis of tetrahydropyrida-
zines (Scheme 1c).<sup>12</sup> Despite these achievements, additional
efforts for their efficient synthesis are highly desirable.
Allenes are useful building blocks for the synthesis of pharma-
ceuticals, natural products, and functional materials.<sup>13,14</sup> A variety
of methods for the eficient synthesis of diferent kinds of allenes
have been well developed.<sup>14</sup> Transition-metal–catalysed reactions of
propargylic alcohol derivatives with various reagents represent one
of the most useful and efficient methodologies for synthesizing
allenes (Scheme 1d).<sup>15</sup> In this context, we set out in the current
work to develop an efficient palladium-catalysed alleneamination

Next, the scope of propargylic acetates 2 was investigated by
reacting them with 1a (Scheme 3). Regardless of the electronic
nature of the para-substituents on the aryl ring, functionalized
propargylic acetates reacted well with hydrazone 1a and pro-
duced a range of allene-containing tetrahydropyridazine deri-
vatives 4a–4g with good results (50–79% yields). When the
substituents were located at a meta- or ortho-position, the
desired tetrahydropyridazine products formed successfully,
although steric effects could not be ignored (4h, 77%; 4i,
41%). Furthermore, 2-naphthyl, cyclohexeyl, cyclopropyl, and
heterocycles like thiophene and quinoline were well tolerated,
affording products 4j–4n in 42–70% yields. Interestingly, the
propargylic acetates bearing a cyclic system were also applic-
able to the current transformation, and the desired products
4p–4r were afforded in 50–73% yields. To demonstrate the
potential applications of this method, fenofibrate derivative
propargylic acetate were also tested, which produced the
desired coupling product 4s in 55% yield.

To prove the practicality of this approach, a gram-scale
reaction was attempted. A 5.0-mmol-scale reaction of
\gamma ,
d-unsaturated hydrazone 1a with propargylic acetate 2a pro-
ceeded smoothly, afording 1.19 g of 3a with an acceptable yield
of 66% (Scheme 4a). The potential applicability of the system
was further illustrated by the good results of the transforma-
tions of 3a, such as a 5-endo cyclization reaction with TfOH and
oxidation of the allene group (Scheme 4b). In addition, the use
of a KMnO oxidation system allowed allene 3a to be used to
form ketone 6 in 77% yield.
On the basis of the previous reports and the experimental
results,<sup>17</sup> a plausible reaction mechanism is proposed
(Scheme 5). First, the oxidative addition of propargylic acetates
to Pd(0) generates a Pd(II) complex II. Subsequently, deprotona-
tion of 1a and ligand exchange give intermediate III, which
then undergoes a migratory insertion to provide complex IV
(path a). Alternatively, coordination of alkene to Pd(II) complex
II afords III<sup>0</sup>, followed by attack of alkene by the deprotonated

In conclusion, we developed an eficient palladium-
catalysed alleneamination reaction, which provides an eficient

To prove the practicality of this approach, a gram-scale
reaction was attempted. A 5.0-mmol-scale reaction of
\gamma ,
d-unsaturated hydrazone 1a with propargylic acetate 2a pro-
ceeded smoothly, afording 1.19 g of 3a with an acceptable yield
of 66% (Scheme 4a). The potential applicability of the system
was further illustrated by the good results of the transforma-
tions of 3a, such as a 5-endo cyclization reaction with TfOH and
oxidation of the allene group (Scheme 4b). In addition, the use
of a KMnO oxidation system allowed allene 3a to be used to
form ketone 6 in 77% yield.
On the basis of the previous reports and the experimental
results,<sup>17</sup> a plausible reaction mechanism is proposed
(Scheme 5). First, the oxidative addition of propargylic acetates
to Pd(0) generates a Pd(II) complex II. Subsequently, deprotona-
tion of 1a and ligand exchange give intermediate III, which
then undergoes a migratory insertion to provide complex IV
(path a). Alternatively, coordination of alkene to Pd(II) complex
II afords III<sup>0</sup>, followed by attack of alkene by the deprotonated
hydrazone moiety to obtain intermediate IV (path b). Finally,
reductive elimination of complex IV afords the corresponding
product 3a, and regenerates the Pd(0) catalyst for the
catalytic cycle.

In conclusion, we developed an eficient palladium-
catalysed alleneamination reaction, which provides an eficient
and practical approach for the synthesis of allene-bearing
tetrahydropyridazines in moderate to good yields. A variety of
readily available g,d-unsaturated hydrazones and functiona-
lized propargylic acetates as starting materials demonstrated
good tolerance. This protocol features a simple catalytic system,
a broad substrate scope, easy scalability, and versatile transfor-
mations. Further investigation on the asymmetry of the trans-
formation is currently underway.
